Manx: hie fin as oshin magh dy helg
English: fin and oshin went out to hunt

Manx: lesh sheshaght trean as moddee elg
English: with a noble train of men and dogs

Manx: cha row un dooinney sloo na keead
English: not less in number than one hundred men

Manx: coshee cha bieau cha row ny lheid
English: so swift and keen none were their like

Manx: lesh feedyn coo eisht hie ad magh
English: with scores of bandogs fierce they sallied forth

Manx: trooid slieau as coan dy yannoo cragh
English: o'er hill and dale much havoc for to make

Manx: quoi daag ad ec y thie agh orree beg
English: #name

Manx: cadley dy kiune fo scadoon'n creg
English: who slept secure beneath the shadowy rock

Manx: slane three feed quallian aeg gyn unnane sloo
English: full three score greyhounds with their whelps they left

Manx: lesh three feed cailleeyn dy yeeaghyn moo
English: with three score old dames to attend the young

Manx: dooyrt 'neen fin ayns craid as corree
English: says fin's fair daughter in disdain and scorn

Manx: kys yiow mayd nish cooilleen er orree'
English: how on young orree shall we be revenged'

Manx: dooyrt inneen oshin 'kiangle mayd eh
English: says oshin's daughter

Manx: lesh folt y ching chionn gys y clea
English: fast to the harrows we will tie his hair

Manx: as cur mayd aile gys y chass cha bieau'
English: and to his nimble feet we'll set a train of fire'

Manx: clysht tappee eisht hug orree ass
English: then up starts orree with a nimble spring

Manx: tra dennee eh'n smuir roie ass e chass
English: feeling his feet a broiling with the heat

Manx: loo mollaght mynney ad dy stroie
English: with curses direful vowing to destroy

Manx: va er n'yannoo craid er mac y ree
English: those who presumed to affront a king his son

Manx: dy farbagh breearey ry ghrian as eayst
English: swearing most bitterly to sun and moon

Manx: dy losht ad hene as thie-yn neesht
English: to burn themselves and all their habitations

Manx: hie orree beg magh dys ny sleityn
English: -then to the mountain hies he fast away

Manx: as speih mooar connee er e geayltyn
English: his heavy gorse-hack poised upon his shoulders

Manx: hoght bart mooar trome hug eh lesh cart
English: eight ponderous burthens thence he carried off

Manx: hoght kionnanyn currit ayns dagh bart
English: and eight large faggots cram'd in ilka burthen

Manx: hoght deiney lheid's 'sy theihll nish t'ayn
English: not eight such men as in the world are now

Manx: cha droggagh bart jeh shoh ny v'ayn
English: could from the ground one of these burthens raise

Manx: ayns dagh uinnag hug eh bart as ayns dagh dorrys
English: into each window he a burthen thrust

Manx: agh mean y thie mooar hene yn bart mooar sollys va fin as oshin nish shelg dy chionn lesh ooilley nyn treanee ayns ollish as joan yaagh wooar ren sheeyney ass y neear troggal ayns bodjallyn agglagh myr rere roie fin as roie oshin derrey d'aase oshin skee agh she fin mooar hene chum sodjey nish roie eisht dylllee fin huggey lesh coraa trome cha vel faagit ain nish agh tholtanyn lhomme quoi ren yn assee shoh nagh re orree beg va'r chosney voue chelleerid gys ooig fo yn chreg raad plooghit lesh yaagh hayrn ad magh er y chass
English: but the grand blazing burthen on the floor
